html:
The Garamantes were a people who built a kingdom in the Fezzan, in the Sahara of southern Libya, from about 500 BCE to about 700 CE, with their capital at Garama, now Germa.

They farmed oases in the desert by digging foggaras, underground channels that tapped ancient groundwater, and grew wheat, barley and dates. They lived in towns and buried their dead in pyramids. The Greek historian Herodotus described them as riding four-horse chariots.

They traded with the Roman cities of the coast, such as Leptis Magna, sending slaves, gold and ivory north. They were among the first to organise trade across the Sahara. When the fossil water ran low, their kingdom faded, around the time of the Arab conquest.
sum: The Garamantes were a people who built a kingdom in the Fezzan, in the Sahara of southern Libya, from about 500 BCE to about 700 CE, with their capital at Garama, now Germa.
